commenti.body: You want to make a Letterboxd account and curate a selection of followers who write those pieces. Not everyone just posts one-liners... there are a lot of users who write long and thoughtful analyses that assume their readers have also seen the movie. I really love this aspect of the site.

MUBI Notebook, Cineaste Magazine, Film Comment, and Senses of Cinema all provide what you're looking for to some degree or another. They don't cover every movie systematically, but they are more likely to have in-depth writing about recent movies than newspaper critics (and their online counterparts). In most cases you'll still have to wait at least a couple months for them to write about something (unless one of their critics saw it at a festival).

I've been planning on doing that for a long time. My area of specialty is 20th century cinema. I don't see new movies as often as I watch older films so I wasn't planning on critiquing new movies. I certainly could. I didn't think there would be any interest

Wordpress is your friend. That's where all the very low-key but hardworking film reviewers are. And I think they're spreading to places like substack and other services which offer paid features.

I recommend googling a niche film that you like with the words " film analysis site:wordpress.com "

Do this once and you'll find at least five incredible reviewers with or without an audience and a butt-ton of hard work.

Bright Wall/Dark Room tilts towards retrospective considerations, but they do often run pieces about relatively recent releases (and have an annual best of the year theme). 

Film Colossus often feels a little self-important to me, but they do in-depth coverage of recent releases (and older ones). 

And it's worth keeping an eye on critics like Matt Zoller Seitz, who publishes frequently on Roger Ebert or Vulture. Some outlets like that will have an official review — the one for folks considering seeing a movie — but then run one or more considerations a week or two into something's run if a critic has something more to say about it.

I do love reading analysis, but a lot of the best stuff these days kinda just ends up on YouTube. You are free to ignore these if they aren’t your thing at all. 

In/Frame/Out does really good incisive film analysis, new and old. 

https://www.youtube.com/@inframeout

Indietrix is the phenomenal video essayist Will Webb, although he actually gets paid for his stuff these days so his channel has slowed down. 

https://www.youtube.com/@Indietrix

The Cinema Cartography does really insightful longer form stuff, again, new and old. 

https://www.youtube.com/@TheCinemaCartography/videos

Dom Noble looks at film adaptations of books. He’s a lot of fun if that’s your thing. 

https://www.youtube.com/@Dominic-Noble

Every Frame a Painting are basically the kings of YouTube film video essay and recently reappeared on the scene after 8 years. No new stuff yet, but it’s inevitable. 

https://www.youtube.com/@everyframeapainting

I haven’t actually watched many videos by Like Stories of Old, but they are great from what I’ve seen, and I really must rectify that. 

https://www.youtube.com/@LikeStoriesofOld/videos

I also haven’t watched many by Eyebrow Cinema, but again, what I have seems good, and I mean to rectify that. 

https://www.youtube.com/@EyebrowCinema

Adequate Emily is phenomenal. Maybe not what you’re looking for but worth your time. 

https://www.youtube.com/@AdequateEmily

No idea what this one is, I think someone else dropped it. Yeah. That’s it. Might be good? Who’s to say? Not me. 

https://www.youtube.com/@profoundunderdog

Dunno why you are getting downvoted for this, many good real life critics use the site to post excellent reviews, and many others (including me when I’m not burnt out) like to post longer reviews. Can definitely add my +1 to LB and following critics/good reviewers. If you block out the annoying big joke reviewers like Lucy and Karsten things really start getting better. I don’t do it anymore, but I used to block all joke reviews until the top 3 on a particular page for the movie were actual in depth or thoughtful reviews.
Do you maybe have any accounts that you would recommend? That write good and thoughtful analyses

Honestly, a bunch of my favorites have only a hundred or so people following, and I'm having a hard time figuring out how to single out small accounts on this forum without it feeling strangely invasive. So I'll say this: I've curated what I think is a great collection of people to follow, so if you go to the Following tab on [my account](https://boxd.it/24dqX), you can dig through a bunch of gems. Not all of them post the kinds of reviews OP asks for, but many do.
Thank you so much! I will definitely check it out! Thanks!
